questions.q: What does the summary say you should do about the broken system?
a: Learn to navigate it instead of fighting it
Work to reform it from the inside
Ignore it and wait for change
Compete for its biggest rewards
questions.why: Lesson 1 says success comes from accepting the world as it is and becoming resourceful.

questions.q: What does the summary say will actually save you?
a: Facing the fact that nobody else will
Finding a powerful mentor
Winning support from family
Waiting for better circumstances
questions.why: Lesson 2 says accepting that no one is coming to rescue you is what sets you free.

questions.q: What benefit of journaling does the summary mention?
a: It filters your thoughts and gives perspective
It records achievements for your resume
It replaces the need for a plan
It keeps you accountable to friends
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends writing down what is on your mind to see the bigger picture.

questions.q: What does the summary say comes with pursuing success?
a: Loneliness and constant challenges
Immediate recognition from peers
A stable and predictable routine
Fewer decisions to make each day
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that friends may drift away and obstacles will keep disrupting your plan.

questions.q: How does the summary suggest identifying your strengths?
a: Taking tests like Strengths Finder and Myers-Briggs
Copying the routines of successful people
Asking friends to list your weaknesses
Waiting for a career crisis to force a choice
questions.why: Lesson 3 names those two assessments as accurate ways to learn where to build.
